author: staurum
text:
I'm given a spare time, so i feel this is best used to dump some mind poos off the bottleneck of my head into my own journal.

A person is only limited by his belief, his imagination. What he sees,
he believes. What he is told, he is suggested. What he is used to,
outside of the norm will feel aliens. Sense of comfort restrains
potential expansion & growth. Diligence inside the known looks
great, however only a few ever questions: does it? A search outside the
boundaries is critiqued and labeled dangerous. Sounds like programming,
does it. People with same programme in mind go together and herd, and
this is contagious.

I, for one, was a person who tend to continue searching for new things,
new answers, new solutions while not realising in doing so there is a
high risk that i'm also letting go the precious things i'm holding. Is
it diligent? is it lazy? Is it pathetic? Is it purposeful? or is it
simply greed? Trying to have everything so that we have every
options/alternatives/answers possible in our hands. Knowing when to
continue expanding and developing is not more important than knowing
when to stop and simply look within. Piano teaches me to self-practice,
but more importantly self-discover the bodily and mind responses i never
 knew before. Health cannot be discovered, investigated, nor bought; it
simply needs to be earned and requires us to work to "deserve" it. So
are other many important things. Often, ignorance still wins.

Everyone has different tenacity in life. The efforts are different, and
sometimes distinguishable. The results are also often (but not always)
different and distinct. Tenacity to make things work is also different
from tenacity to find reasons why things don't work. Great inventors, in
 my view, didnt have much time to elaborate their unsuccessful findings;
 but rather tried to save their lifetime to just find what does work.

One of great learning way is to question everything. Radical honesty, as
 Ray Daiio put it, really is the best way to effective efficient
improvement. One finding to the next finding, one hypothesis to the next
 hypothesis. Testing everything. Working at everything. So time
consuming, so energy draining. Mistakes repeated one after another until
 we stop them. Following and replicating others without personally
investigated reasons is the biggest sin anyone easily commits. Humans
since childhood are so indoctrinated with word "Faith & Belief".
Even the government, social media, giant corporations want all humans in
 the world to stay in the "Faith & Belief" world. Please wake up and
 listen, It is good only for children and the naive. Mature adults
holding this philosophy without personally working to prove it are
simply lazy and will be lost so easily, or worse: "slaughtered,
harvested off".

Time is almost up. Until next "mind-dumping session" time....

Big thanks to IF as always, one of the only few human beings who is way too nice in this world.
